thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGE: High rate of auth anomalies detected on auth-proxy-prod across multiple regions. Alerting on 5xx spikes + suspicious repeated token signatures. Please acknowledge.

maria (oncall-sre): acked, joining. seeing increased 500 responses from auth-proxy and some 200s for old sessions. paging sec-eng.

kevin (sec-eng): on it. initial triage: we have a small sample of logs with repeated Authorization headers that look expired but accepted. suspicious IPs: 45.77.23.0/24 and 2a03:4000::/32 hitting the token endpoint.

oliver (infra): I can throttle those CIDRs at the edge WAF now. preparing rule, will apply to prod-eu first as canary.

kevin (sec-eng): thanks. quick forensics: looks like a token TTL skew bug from auth-service's clock drift + a stale signing key leftover in staging that got included in a debug log push to a customer-facing S3 path earlier today. Logs contain truncated header samples. sample: 

```
2026-03-17T03:24:12Z auth-proxy-prod req=abcd1234 ip=45.77.23.11 method=POST path=/v1/session status=200 user_id=840 auth_header="Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSU...TRUNC"
```

kevin (sec-eng): risk: attacker could replay captured headers to create sessions until tokens are rejected. need immediate containment.

maria (oncall-sre): mitigation plan proposals: 1) block CIDRs at WAF (oliver), 2) disable S3 log push for affected prefix (oliver), 3) bump token version / rotate signing key and issue short-lived revocation flag (kevin), 4) customers page/comms (jamie). agree?

oliver (infra): WAF rule pushed to prod-eu as canary: rule id wf-4729, blocking 45.77.23.0/24. applying to prod-us now. disabling logrun for bucket s3://redwood-logs/session-debug/ by removing the delivery policy.

jamie (pm-custops): starting incident comms draft. need list of impacted customers (kevin/maria please confirm). will prep temporary status page blurb: "We detected suspicious auth activity; we have contained the issue and rotated keys; customers may need to relogin."

kevin (sec-eng): token rotation plan: roll new signing key into auth-service and increment token version header (x-token-v=2). Tokens with v=1 will be invalidated after a 10m overlap once the auth-service starts enforcing. deploy sequence: canary auth-service-2 in prod-eu, then prod-us. command to start key rollout: 

```
# deploy new key to auth-service config
kubectl set env deployment/auth-service AUTH_SIGNING_KEY_ID=new-key-20260317 -n prod
# flip enforcement config
kubectl set env deployment/auth-service TOKEN_MIN_VERSION=2 -n prod
```

maria (oncall-sre): performing the canary now with a single replica in prod-eu. monitoring error budget and customer-facing endpoints.

legal-bot: Note: if PII/credentials were copied to public S3 objects, escalate to legal and compliance. start retention and access logs preservation.

kevin (sec-eng): confirmed log push included truncated headers but not full PII. still treating as sensitive. adv: execute immediate key rotation and schedule audit of who accessed the S3 prefix during window 02:00-04:00 UTC.

maria (oncall-sre): canary looks okay after 3m. no increase in 5xx, token rejects for v=1 are in effect for canary. proceeding to roll to prod-us.

oliver (infra): WAF rules are active globally. we've also added a short-term rate-limit on /v1/session to 10r/s per IP for 1h.

jamie (pm-custops): comms draft ready, holding until rotation completes. we'll send targeted emails to customers with sessions active in that time window.

maria (oncall-sre): rolling key to all regions now. estimated full enforcement in ~8 minutes. setting incident priority P1 and assigning follow-ups: sec-eng for audit, infra for log retention and WAF cleanup, custops for customer notices.

kevin (sec-eng): next steps for forensics: grep logs for the sample window, collect s3 access logs, identify any external downloads of that prefix. I'll start.

jamie (pm-custops): will prepare support playbook for login resets and escalation path.

maria (oncall-sre): good work team. will update status channel once rotation verified and then transition to postmortem. reactions: :white_check_mark: :eyes:
